title: Full first-order formulas and capture-free substitution

based_on.title: Proof Theory 2018: Syntax and semantics of predicate logic; Natural Deduction (handout 8)

summary: Retain all constructive first-order connectives, define capture-free scope substitution, and connect the full trees to the existing classical syntax.
abstract: A proof that something exists can contain a witness, while a proof that its nonexistence is impossible may contain no such term. Classical truth identifies these assertions, so a compact classical formula alphabet need not preserve the distinctions needed to study constructive proofs. We keep conjunction, disjunction and existential quantification as separate constructors and distinguish free parameters from quantified slots. One substitution operation then handles renaming, replacement and opening a quantified body without capture. Its composition and truth laws explain how these operations fit together, and a precise expansion recovers the existing classical formulas without identifying their different full proof trees.
